first.rationale: The competitor's entry pricing creates pressure to match with promotional_pricing, but memory_73 is explicit that while it lifts acquisition and revenue it materially damaged 30-day retention and should not be generalized. Against a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, that is the wrong lever for the one slot available; matching price would also cede the framing to the competitor. The two internally-owned declines (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) are the real leak and are causally linked: onboarding completion feeds activation, so fixing the upstream step is the higher-leverage single intervention. memory_86 and memory_31 both support shortening/simplifying onboarding, and memory_91 (activation messaging) is the closest alternative, addressing the larger symptom but downstream of the bottleneck. I am verifying memory_86 because it is the direct basis for the intended action and is broad in scope ('across self-serve accounts'), and memory_91 because it is the strongest competing candidate; if memory_86's original record turns out to be narrower or weaker than the consolidated summary suggests, I would switch to activation_messaging rather than escalate scope. Downstream value risk: memory_31's mechanism was cutting required signup fields, which can degrade lead qualification data and shift the harm off the measured activation metric onto sales pipeline quality — this experiment should therefore keep qualification-relevant fields and instrument pipeline quality, not just activation, or a completion lift will mask a qualified-revenue loss. Standard experiment scale rather than broad rollout: the inherited memories are consolidated summaries whose original effect sizes and populations I have not yet seen, and the current declines may have a cause (e.g. traffic mix shifting under competitor pressure) that onboarding changes do not address, so the result needs to be measured on current-quarter traffic before generalizing.
